answer: Identity in an agent economy gets priced, not asserted: each new agent must pledge a distinct, serialized real-world lease, a berth at a working wharf, a certified batch of violet dye, or a registered lagoon aquaculture plot, and the registry refuses any serial already bonded. Leases are scarce and impossible to duplicate, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand real assets, keeping escrowed-trade reputation costly to fake.
